name: ROCr runtime refuses kernel dispatches declaring hostcall buffers when PCIe root port lacks AtomicOps, causing all RCCL collectives to fail
symptom: When initializing multi-GPU inference with RCCL/vLLM on consumer motherboards or virtualized setups (VFIO/KVM), all RCCL collective operations fail at kernel dispatch. The ROCr runtime refuses any kernel execution that declares a hostcall buffer.
root_cause: The PCIe root port or bridge above the consumer GPU fails to advertise PCIe 3.0/4.0 AtomicOps capability. The ROCr runtime strictly requires AtomicOps to allocate and manage hostcall buffers used by RCCL collectives for multi-GPU synchronization. If the root port does not advertise AtomicOps, dispatch is rejected by the runtime.
workaround: On bare metal, enable PCIe AtomicOps, ACS, and ReBAR in the motherboard BIOS (and update BIOS firmware). On virtual machines (QEMU/KVM/VFIO), configure the root PCIe port with AtomicOps routing/forwarding enabled (e.g. qemu host bridge flags) so the guest kernel can see root port AtomicOps support.
notes: Documented in dual-radeon-vllm and reported in ROCm issue #6520; reproduced on both bare metal consumer boards and virtualized topologies.
